newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks close down on blue-chip fall.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks close down on blue-chip fall.

text.p: Manila stocks finished down on Monday as most blue chips tumbled and punters started taking profits on speculative issues, traders said.

"Some people are starting to get scared of speculatives so we saw a start of profit-taking and hopefully once money comes out of these stocks, blue chips will once again be bought up," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
Traders said Friday's drop of $0.25 to $58.50 in PLDT's American Depositary Receipts led to a sharper decline in PLDT shares on Monday.

Oil and mining issues which remained subdued for some time posted gains. The rest of the indices - commercial-industrial, property, all share and banking - were down. Volume was quite heavy at 13.6 billion shares worth 2.7 billion pesos.
Louie Bate, head of sales at ING Barings, said with the mild technical pullback on Monday, range bound trading may be seen on Tuesday and until more earnings data trickle in.

"This is a well-deserved rest. We are just in a short respite which should give us the foundation to reach an initial resistance of 3,300 later in the week," said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities.
